(a) Write 36% as a fraction in its simplest form.

Consider the following statements.
Statement 1: 7/20 of a quantity is 35% of it.
Statement 2: 0.4% written as a decimal is 0.4.
Statement 3: 27/60 and 9/20 are both ways of writing 45%.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 and 3 only

questions.q:
Two badam drink mixes are on a shop shelf. Their labels give the grams of each ingredient in one pack, and the amount of powder to stir into one glass of milk.
Mix X (200 g pack): sugar 118 g, milk solids 50 g, badam powder 24 g, other 8 g. Use 20 g per glass.
Mix Y (250 g pack): sugar 135 g, milk solids 80 g, badam powder 30 g, other 5 g. Use 25 g per glass.
(a) What percentage of Mix X is sugar?
(b) Mix Y has 6 g more badam powder per pack than Mix X. Does that make Mix Y richer in badam? Use percentages.
(c) What percentage of Mix Y is sugar, and which mix is less sugary gram for gram?
(d) A parent wants the drink that puts less sugar into each glass her child drinks. Which mix should she buy? Use your percentages and the amount per glass.
questions.a: (a) 118/200 x 100 = 59%. (b) No. Badam is 24/200 x 100 = 12% of X and 30/250 x 100 = 12% of Y, so the share is the same; Y has more grams only because its pack is bigger. (c) 135/250 x 100 = 54%, so Mix Y is less sugary gram for gram (54% against 59%). (d) Sugar per glass: X: 59% of 20 g = 11.8 g; Y: 54% of 25 g = 13.5 g. She should buy Mix X: although Y has the smaller sugar share, a glass of Y uses more powder, so it carries more sugar.
s: Part (b): both 12%, so not richer in badam
Part (c): 54%, so Y is less sugary gram for gram
Part (d): 11.8 g against 13.5 g per glass, so Mix X

questions.q: In a class of 40 students, 9 cycle to school, 3/10 of the class walk, and all the others come by bus. The percentage of the class that comes by bus is ___% (write the number in digits).

A rule card on a class wall says: 'To write a fraction as a percentage, find an equivalent fraction with denominator 100. So fractions such as 1/3 and 5/11 cannot be written as percentages.' Check both sentences of the card and give a verdict.
questions.a: Partly right. The first sentence is a correct method (3/4 = 75/100 = 75%). The second is wrong: any fraction can be written as a percentage by multiplying it by 100, and the percentage need not be a whole number. 1/3 x 100 = 33.33...% (33 1/3%) and 5/11 x 100 = 45.45...%.
s: Accepts the first sentence as a correct method
Verdict: partly right, since a percentage need not be a whole number

questions.q: Mango pulp makes up 11/40 of Brand A's drink and 7/25 of Brand B's drink. Which statement about the two drinks is correct?
questions.a: Brand B has more mango: 28% against 27.5%
o: Brand B has more mango: 28% against 27.5%
Brand A has more mango, since 11 parts beat 7
Brand A has more mango: 27.5% against 2.8%
They are equal, since both round to 28%

questions.q: True or False: '0.5% of a bag of rice is the same as half of the bag.' Give a reason.
questions.a: False. 0.5% = 0.5/100 = 1/200 of the bag, which is a tiny amount. Half of the bag is 1/2 = 50%, which is 100 times as much.

questions.q:
A painter mixes white, blue and green paint in the ratio 5 : 2 : 1 to make Shade 1. In Shade 2, blue makes up 3/10 of the paint.
(a) What percentage of Shade 1 is white, blue and green?
(b) How many litres of blue paint are in 6 litres of Shade 1?
(c) Which shade has the larger share of blue? How many more litres of blue are there in 100 litres of that shade than in 100 litres of the other?
(d) He pours 4 litres of Shade 1 and 6 litres of Shade 2 into one drum. What percentage of the drum is blue?
questions.a: (a) Total parts = 8. White 5/8 x 100 = 62.5%, blue 2/8 x 100 = 25%, green 1/8 x 100 = 12.5%. (b) 25% of 6 L = 1.5 L. (c) Shade 2: 3/10 = 30%, against 25% for Shade 1, so Shade 2 has the larger share: 100 L of Shade 2 holds 30 L of blue against 25 L in Shade 1, which is 5 L more. (d) Blue = 25% of 4 L + 30% of 6 L = 1 + 1.8 = 2.8 L out of 10 L, which is 28%.
s: Part (a): 62.5%, 25% and 12.5% from a total of 8 parts
Part (c): Shade 2, with 5 L more blue in every 100 L

A tailor uses 0.125 of a roll of cloth for each kurta he stitches.
(a) What percentage of the roll does one kurta use?
(b) After stitching 5 kurtas, what percentage of the roll is left, and how many more kurtas can he stitch from it?
questions.a: (a) 0.125 x 100 = 12.5% of the roll. (b) 5 kurtas use 5 x 12.5% = 62.5%, so 100% - 62.5% = 37.5% is left, which is enough for 37.5 / 12.5 = 3 more kurtas.
s: Part (b): 37.5% left, enough for 3 more kurtas

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Writing 3/8 as 37.5% and 2/5 as 40% shows at a glance which of the two fractions is larger.
Reason (R): A percentage is a fraction whose denominator is fixed at 100, so any two percentages have the same denominator.
questions.a: A and R are both true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
o: A and R are both true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A and R are both true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q: A club report says: 'Each member plays exactly one indoor game. 3/5 of the members play chess, 45% play carrom and the remaining 0.2 of the members play table tennis.' Show that these figures cannot all be correct.
questions.a: Write all three as percentages: 3/5 = 60%, 45% and 0.2 = 20%. Together they make 60 + 45 + 20 = 125%. Since each member plays exactly one game, the three groups together must make exactly 100% of the members, so 125% is impossible.
s: Explains that the groups must total exactly 100%

questions.q: Four wards report the share of homes with solar panels in different forms. Ward 1: 0.065 of its homes. Ward 2: 6.2%. Ward 3: 13 of every 250 homes. Ward 4: 7/125 of its homes. Which ward has the largest share?
questions.a: Ward 1, as 0.065 is 6.5%
o: Ward 3, as 13 is the largest number

questions.q:
(a) Write 5/8, 0.6 and 31/50 as percentages.
(b) Use your answers to arrange 5/8, 0.6, 61% and 31/50 in increasing order.

A builder makes concrete by mixing cement, sand and gravel by weight in the ratio 1 : 2 : 5. For a stronger slab he could use the ratio 1 : 2 : 4 instead. He needs 3000 kg of concrete for a roof and has only 400 kg of cement left at the site.
(a) What percentage of the 1 : 2 : 5 concrete is gravel?
(b) A mixer drum of 1 : 2 : 5 concrete holds 750 kg of sand. What is the total weight of the concrete in it?
(c) Which of the two ratios can he use to make all 3000 kg with the cement he has? Show the cement each ratio needs.
questions.a: (a) Gravel is 5 of 1 + 2 + 5 = 8 parts: 5/8 x 100 = 62.5%. (b) Sand is 2/8 = 25% of the concrete, so 25% of the total is 750 kg and the total is 750 x 100/25 = 3000 kg. (c) Ratio 1 : 2 : 5: cement is 1/8 = 12.5% of 3000 = 375 kg, which is within 400 kg. Ratio 1 : 2 : 4: cement is 1/7 (about 14.29%) of 3000, about 428.6 kg, more than 400 kg. So he must use 1 : 2 : 5.
s: Part (c): needs 375 kg against about 428.6 kg, so 1 : 2 : 5

questions.q: A percentage z% is equal to the fraction 12/40. The same percentage written as a fraction with numerator 21 is 21/___ (write the number in digits).

In a reading challenge, 27 of the 36 students of Class 8A finished, 0.78 of Class 8B finished, and 31 of the 40 students of Class 8C finished.
(a) Write each class's result as a percentage.
(b) Rank the classes from best to worst result.
(c) How many more students of Class 8A would have had to finish for 8A to have the best result of the three?
questions.a: (a) 8A: 27/36 x 100 = 75%; 8B: 0.78 = 78%; 8C: 31/40 x 100 = 77.5%. (b) 8B (78%), 8C (77.5%), 8A (75%). (c) 8A must beat 78%. 28/36 x 100 = 77.78% is still below 78%, but 29/36 x 100 = 80.56% is above it, so 29 - 27 = 2 more students would have had to finish.
s: Part (c): 2 more (29 of 36 is 80.56%; 28 of 36 is only 77.78%)

questions.q:

questions.q:
In a tea garden, 9 of every 40 bushes are newly planted.
(a) Write this share per decem (per 10), per cent (per 100) and per mille (per 1000).
(b) Which of the three forms gives a whole number here? Explain why, for any share written as k/40 (k a whole number), the per-mille form is always a whole number but the per-cent form is not.
questions.a: (a) 9/40 x 10 = 2.25 per decem; 9/40 x 100 = 22.5 per cent; 9/40 x 1000 = 225 per mille. (b) Per mille. k/40 x 1000 = 25k, a whole number for every whole k, because 1000 is a multiple of 40. But k/40 x 100 = 2.5k, which is a whole number only when k is even, because 100 is not a multiple of 40.
s: Part (b): per mille; 1000/40 = 25 is whole but 100/40 = 2.5 is not

questions.q:
A health office compares how common a skin disease is in three towns. Town P reports it in 0.3% of its people. Town Q reports 2.5 cases per mille (per 1000 people). Town R found 7 cases among 2,000 people checked.
(a) Write the figure for each town as a percentage.
(b) Write the figure for each town per mille.
(c) Rank the towns from the most affected to the least affected.
(d) The office wants to print one figure per town in a report. Which form, per cent or per mille, gives simpler numbers here, and why?
questions.a: (a) P: 0.3%; Q: 2.5 per mille = 2.5/1000 = 0.25%; R: 7/2000 x 100 = 0.35%. (b) P: 0.3% = 3 per mille; Q: 2.5 per mille; R: 7/2000 x 1000 = 3.5 per mille. (c) R (3.5), P (3), Q (2.5). (d) Per mille: the figures 3.5, 3 and 2.5 avoid the small decimals 0.35, 0.3 and 0.25 that per cent gives, because the disease affects far fewer than 1 in 100 people.
s: Part (d): per mille, since the rates are well below 1 in 100

questions.q: A student's working reads: '9/24 x 100 = 37.5% and 0.4 x 100 = 40%, so the second share is larger, by 2.5 out of every 100.' Write a real situation that this working answers. Say what each share measures, and explain why the student could not compare 9/24 and 0.4 directly as written.
questions.a: Example: in Class 8A, 9 of the 24 students play a musical instrument, and in Class 8B 0.4 of the students do. As percentages, 9/24 = 37.5% and 0.4 = 40%, so a larger share of 8B plays (2.5 more students in every 100). As written, one share is a fraction with denominator 24 and the other a decimal; turning both into percentages puts them on the same denominator of 100, so they can be compared. Any situation in which 9 of 24 is compared with a share of 0.4 is acceptable.
s: A situation with a share of 9 out of 24 and a share of 0.4
Says each percentage is the part of its own group, 37.5% and 40%
Explains that converting to percentages gives both the denominator 100

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
Statement 1: 150% of 60 is 60 + 50 = 110.
Statement 2: If 30% of k is 72, then 90% of k is 216.
Statement 3: A percentage greater than 100% is always a mistake, because a part cannot be more than the whole.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 2 only

A farmer harvested 260 kg of groundnuts last year and 650 kg this year. A local news report says, 'This year's harvest is 250% more than last year's.' Is the report correct? Explain.
questions.a: No. This year's harvest is 650/260 x 100 = 250% OF last year's harvest (2.5 times it). The increase is 650 - 260 = 390 kg, which is 390/260 x 100 = 150% of last year's harvest, so the harvest is 150% more, not 250% more.
s: Verdict: no, '250% of' was mistaken for '250% more'

questions.q: A cyclist riding from Pune to Satara has covered 35% of the route, which is 63 km. How many kilometres are still left?
questions.a: 117 km

questions.q:
A 140 g packet of chikki is 45% jaggery.
(a) Complete the proportion 45 : 100 :: ___ : 140 and find the mass of jaggery in the packet.
(b) A 180 g packet of another brand is 40% jaggery. Which packet has more jaggery, and by how many grams?
questions.a: (a) 45/100 = j/140, so j = 45/100 x 140 = 63 g. (b) 40% of 180 = 0.4 x 180 = 72 g. The 180 g packet has 72 - 63 = 9 g more jaggery, even though its percentage is lower.
s: Part (b): 72 g, so the 180 g packet, by 9 g

questions.q:
On a school trip, 60% of the students are from Grade 8 and the rest are from Grade 9. Half of the Grade 8 students are girls. There are 24 Grade 9 girls, and they make up one quarter of the Grade 9 students on the trip.
(a) How many Grade 9 students are on the trip?
(b) How many students are on the trip in all?
(c) What percentage of all the students on the trip are girls?
(d) A teacher says, 'Half of Grade 8 and a quarter of Grade 9 are girls, so the girls are (50% + 25%) / 2 = 37.5% of the trip.' Explain why this is wrong, and find what percentage of the girls on the trip are from Grade 8.
questions.a: (a) 24 is 25% of the Grade 9 students, so there are 24 x 4 = 96 Grade 9 students. (b) Grade 9 is 100% - 60% = 40% of the trip, so 40% of the total is 96 and the total is 96 x 100/40 = 240. (c) Grade 8 has 60% of 240 = 144 students, of whom 72 are girls. Girls = 72 + 24 = 96, and 96/240 x 100 = 40%. (d) Averaging 50% and 25% treats the two grades as equal in size, but Grade 8 (144) is larger than Grade 9 (96), so its 50% counts for more and the true share, 40%, is above 37.5%. Grade 8 girls are 72/96 x 100 = 75% of the girls.
s: Part (d): averaging ignores the unequal grade sizes; 75% of the girls are from Grade 8

questions.q: If 60% of a number n is 222, then 35% of n is ___ (write the number in digits).

A district office keeps the normal monsoon rainfall for each month and compares it with this year's rain.
Month | Normal rainfall | This year
June | 160 mm | 136 mm
July | 240 mm | 130% of normal
August | 200 mm | 0.9 of normal
September | 120 mm | forecast 140 mm
(a) What percentage of the June normal fell this June?
(b) How many millimetres of rain fell in July?
(c) How many millimetres fell in August?
(d) Suppose the September forecast comes true. A news report calls the season 'above normal' because the June to September total beats the normal total. A farmer whose paddy needs at least 90% of the normal rain in every month says the season was poor for him. Use percentages to judge each view.
questions.a: (a) 136/160 x 100 = 85%. (b) 130% of 240 = 1.3 x 240 = 312 mm. (c) 0.9 x 200 = 180 mm. (d) Normal total = 160 + 240 + 200 + 120 = 720 mm; this year 136 + 312 + 180 + 140 = 768 mm, which is 768/720 x 100 = 106.67% of normal, so the report is right about the season as a whole. But June had only 85% of its normal (August had 90%, July 130%, September 116.67%), so June fell below the 90% the paddy needs. Both are right: the large July and September rains hide a dry June in the total.
s: Part (d): total 106.67% of normal, but June only 85%, so both views hold

questions.q: True or False: 'If a shop's sales are 125% of its target, then the target is 80% of the sales.' Give a reason.
questions.a: True. Sales = 1.25 x target, so target = sales / 1.25 = 0.8 x sales = 80% of the sales. For example, a target of Rs 4,000 and sales of Rs 5,000: 4000/5000 x 100 = 80%.
s: Shows target = sales / 1.25 = 0.8 of sales, or checks with numbers

questions.q: For a recycling drive, School A set a target of 400 kg of old newspaper and collected 540 kg. School B set a target of 500 kg and collected 630 kg. Which school did better against its own target?
questions.a: School A: 135% of target against 126%
o: School B: it collected 90 kg more than A
Neither: a share above 100% is a mistake

questions.q: In a hall of 200 people, 98% are wearing school uniform. Some parents, none in uniform, now walk in, and nobody leaves. After that, people in uniform make up 80% of those in the hall. How many parents walked in? Show your reasoning.
questions.a: At first, 98% of 200 = 196 people wear uniform. Nobody in uniform leaves or enters, so the 196 stay and are now 80% of the hall. If 196 is 80% of the total, the total is 196 x 100/80 = 245 people. So 245 - 200 = 45 parents walked in.
s: Finds 196 people in uniform, a number that does not change
Uses 196 = 80% of the new total to get 245 people

questions.q:
750 students voted to choose a site for the eco-club's tree planting. Every student chose exactly one of three sites. Site A got 38% of the votes, Site B got 288 votes and Site C got the remaining votes. The club's rule: a site wins only if it gets more than 40% of the votes; otherwise a second vote is held between the two sites with the most votes.
(a) How many votes did Site A get?
(b) What percentage of the votes did Site B get?
(c) How many votes, and what percentage, did Site C get?
(d) Does any site win straight away? If not, which two sites go to the second vote?
questions.a: (a) 38% of 750 = 0.38 x 750 = 285 votes. (b) 288/750 x 100 = 38.4%. (c) 750 - 285 - 288 = 177 votes, which is 177/750 x 100 = 23.6%. (d) No site has more than 40% (the highest is Site B with 38.4%), so a second vote is held between Site B (38.4%) and Site A (38%).
s: Part (d): no winner; second vote between B and A

questions.q:
Assertion (A): If 40% of a journey is 92 km, then 20% of the same journey is 46 km.
Reason (R): y% of a quantity is found by multiplying the quantity by the whole number y itself, without dividing by 100.
questions.a: A is true but R is false.
o: A is true but R is false.
A and R are both true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A and R are both true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q:
(a) A school day lasts 7 hours 12 minutes. What percentage of a whole day (24 hours) is it?
(b) Lab periods take 25% of the school day. Without first finding the minutes, say what percentage of the whole day is spent in labs, then check your answer in minutes.
questions.a: (a) 7 h 12 min = 7.2 hours, and 7.2/24 x 100 = 30% of a day. (b) 25% of 30% = 0.25 x 0.30 = 0.075 = 7.5% of the whole day. Check: 7.5% of 1440 minutes = 108 minutes, and 25% of the 432-minute school day is also 108 minutes.

questions.q: Write a word problem about a real situation in which 35% of a whole is 84, and the question asks for the part that is LEFT. Then solve your problem.
questions.a: Example: a water tank is being filled, and the 84 litres poured in so far are 35% of its capacity. How many more litres are needed to fill it? Capacity = 84 x 100/35 = 240 L, so 240 - 84 = 156 L more are needed. Any situation where 84 is 35% of a whole and the remaining 65% (156) is asked for is acceptable.
s: A situation where 84 is 35% of a whole

questions.q: Without working out either value in full, decide which is larger: 48% of 260, or 26% of 480?
questions.a: They are equal, both being 124.8
o: It cannot be decided without full working

questions.q:
A bar model for a water tank marks 0% at one end and 100% at 2,400 litres.
(a) How many litres sit at the 15% mark?
(b) A bigger tank holds 3,000 litres. At what percentage mark of this bar would 3,000 litres fall?
questions.a: (a) 15% of 2400 = 0.15 x 2400 = 360 L. (b) 3000/2400 x 100 = 125%, so it falls beyond the 100% mark, a quarter of the bar further on.

questions.q:
A garment unit has a target of 2,400 shirts a week. In Week 1 it made 1,860 shirts. In Week 2 it made 112.5% of the target. In Week 3 it fell 30% short of the target.
(a) What percentage of the target was made in Week 1?
(b) How many shirts were made in Week 2?
(c) How many shirts were made in Week 3?
(d) What percentage of the three-week target was made in the three weeks together? (Round to two decimal places.)
(e) How many shirts must Week 4 produce for the four weeks together to meet exactly 100% of the four-week target, and what percentage of a weekly target is that?
s: Part (e): 3,360 shirts, 140% of a weekly target

questions.q:
Put >, < or = in each blank and justify.
(a) 29% of 410 ___ 41% of 290 (decide without multiplying)
(b) 45% of 300 ___ 30% of 440
s: Part (a): = , since both equal 29 x 41 x 10 / 100

questions.q: After entry fees were raised, the average daily footfall at Museum A fell from 640 to 480 visitors and at Museum B from 900 to 700 visitors. Which statement correctly compares the two percentage falls?
questions.a: Museum A: 25% against 22.22%
o: Museum B: it lost 200 visitors, not 160
Neither: both fell by about a quarter

questions.q: The price of 1 kg of onions rose from Rs 32 to Rs 44 in a month. Tomatoes cost Rs 40 a kg at the start of the month, and their price rose by the same percentage. Tomatoes now cost Rs ___ a kg (write the number in digits).

Riya wrote three science tests with different maximum marks. She scored 39 out of 52, then 48 out of 64, then 57 out of 75. Her coach says, 'Your second result was exactly as good as your first, and your third was better than both.' Is the coach right? Justify with percentages.
questions.a: Yes, the coach is right. Test 1: 39/52 x 100 = 75%. Test 2: 48/64 x 100 = 75%. Test 3: 57/75 x 100 = 76%. The first two are equal, even though her marks rose from 39 to 48, and the third (76%) is higher than both. Raw marks cannot be compared because the maximum marks differ.
s: Verdict: right; equal, then better, judged by percentages and not by raw marks

questions.q:
A 150 g packet of namkeen M has 12 g of salt; a 200 g packet of namkeen N has 15 g of salt.
(a) What percentage of each packet is salt?
(b) N has more grams of salt. Is N the saltier snack? Explain using (a).
questions.a: (a) M: 12/150 x 100 = 8%. N: 15/200 x 100 = 7.5%. (b) No. N has more salt only because its packet is bigger; each gram of M has more salt (8% against 7.5%), so M is saltier.
s: Part (b): no, M is saltier because its share of salt is larger

questions.q: A report says, 'Sales of bicycles in our town fell by 60% over five years.' This year 2,400 bicycles were sold. How many were sold five years ago?
True or False: 'Kunal scored 40 marks out of 100 in the first test and 50 marks out of 100 in the second, so the percentage increase in his marks is 10%.' Give a reason.
questions.a: False. His marks rose by 10, from 40 to 50. The percentage increase is (amount of increase / original amount) x 100 = 10/40 x 100 = 25%, not 10%. The 10 is the rise in marks, not the rise as a percentage of what he had.

questions.q:
A family buys the same vegetables every week. The vendor's prices per kg last month and this month were:
Tomatoes: Rs 36 then Rs 45
Onions: Rs 40 then Rs 46
Potatoes: Rs 25 then Rs 24
Beans: Rs 80 then Rs 96
Each week the family buys 2 kg tomatoes, 3 kg onions, 5 kg potatoes and 1 kg beans.
(a) Find the percentage change in the price of each vegetable.
(b) Which vegetable rose the most in rupees, and which rose the most as a percentage?
(c) Find the family's weekly bill last month and this month, and its percentage change. (Round to two decimal places.)
(d) The vendor says, 'On average my prices went up by (25 + 15 - 4 + 20) / 4 = 14%.' Explain why the family's bill went up by less than 14%.
questions.a: (a) Tomatoes: 9/36 x 100 = 25% increase. Onions: 6/40 x 100 = 15% increase. Potatoes: 1/25 x 100 = 4% decrease. Beans: 16/80 x 100 = 20% increase. (b) Beans rose the most in rupees (Rs 16), but tomatoes rose the most as a percentage (25%). (c) Last month: 2 x 36 + 3 x 40 + 5 x 25 + 80 = Rs 397. This month: 2 x 45 + 3 x 46 + 5 x 24 + 96 = Rs 444. Change = 47/397 x 100 = 11.84% increase. (d) The 14% treats every vegetable as equally important. The family spends most on potatoes (5 kg), whose price fell, and buys only 1 kg of beans, so the falls and small rises count for more of the bill than the simple average assumes.
s: Part (b): beans in rupees, tomatoes as a percentage
Part (c): Rs 397 to Rs 444, an 11.84% increase
Part (d): the average ignores how many kg of each are bought

questions.q: Tara scored 51 out of 60 in Maths and 66 out of 80 in Hindi. In which subject did she do better, and why?
questions.a: Maths: 85% against 82.5%
o: Neither: the totals are not equal

questions.q:
After a 15% increase, a school's enrolment is 1,380 students.
(a) What was the enrolment before the increase?
(b) By what percentage must the enrolment now fall to return to the old number? (Round to two decimal places.)
(c) Why is the answer to (b) not 15%?
questions.a: (a) 115% of the old enrolment = 1380, so old = 1380 x 100/115 = 1,200. (b) Fall needed = 180, and 180/1380 x 100 = 13.04%. (c) The fall is measured against the new, larger number 1,380, while the rise was measured against 1,200; the same 180 students is a smaller share of the bigger base.
s: Part (c): the base changes from 1,200 to 1,380

questions.q:
An election officer compares voter turnout in three wards.
Ward | Registered voters | Votes cast
Ward 1 | 4,800 | 3,240
Ward 2 | 6,250 | 4,500
Ward 3 | 3,600 | 2,610
In the previous election, Ward 1 had 4,500 registered voters and a turnout of 60%.
(a) What was the turnout (votes cast as a percentage of registered voters) in Ward 1 this time?
(b) By what percentage did the number of votes cast in Ward 1 increase since the previous election?
(c) Arrange the three wards from highest to lowest turnout this time.
(d) A 'best turnout' prize goes to the ward with the highest turnout percentage. Ward 2 says it should win because it cast the most votes. Who wins? How many more votes would Ward 2 have needed to beat the winner's turnout?
questions.a: (a) 3240/4800 x 100 = 67.5%. (b) Previous votes cast = 60% of 4,500 = 2,700. Increase = 540, and 540/2700 x 100 = 20%. (c) Ward 2: 4500/6250 x 100 = 72%; Ward 3: 2610/3600 x 100 = 72.5%. Order: Ward 3 (72.5%), Ward 2 (72%), Ward 1 (67.5%). (d) Ward 3 wins (72.5% against 72%). Ward 2 cast more votes only because it has more registered voters. To beat 72.5%, Ward 2 needed more than 72.5% of 6,250 = 4,531.25 votes, that is at least 4,532 votes, or 32 more than its 4,500.
s: Part (d): Ward 3 wins; Ward 2 needed 32 more votes (4,532)

questions.q:
'The population of a district in 2011 was 140% of its population in 1991.'
(a) Write this as a statement about percentage increase.
(b) If the 2011 population was 4.2 crore, what was the 1991 population?
questions.a: (a) The population increased by 40% from 1991 to 2011. (b) 1.4 x (1991 population) = 4.2 crore, so the 1991 population = 4.2 / 1.4 = 3 crore.

questions.q:
A housing society ran a campaign to save water. Its daily water use fell from 48,000 L to 40,800 L. Block A's use fell from 18,000 L to 14,400 L, and Block B's fell from 30,000 L to 26,400 L. The society had aimed for a 20% cut overall.
(a) By what percentage did the society's daily water use fall?
(b) How many more litres a day must the society save to reach its 20% aim?
(c) Find the percentage cut made by each block.
(d) Both blocks saved the same number of litres. The society gives its award to the block with the larger percentage cut. Which block wins, and why is the percentage the fairer measure here?
questions.a: (a) Fall = 7,200 L, and 7200/48000 x 100 = 15%. (b) A 20% cut means using 80% of 48,000 = 38,400 L, so it must save 40,800 - 38,400 = 2,400 L more a day. (c) Block A: 3600/18000 x 100 = 20%. Block B: 3600/30000 x 100 = 12%. (d) Block A wins. Each block saved 3,600 L, but Block A used much less to begin with, so the same saving is a larger share (20% against 12%) of its own use.
s: Part (d): Block A, as the same saving is a larger share of its smaller use

questions.q: A shop cuts the price of a fan from Rs 800 to Rs 680 and advertises it as 'a 17.6% price cut'. Check the advertisement.

s: Verdict: wrong; 17.6% uses the new price as the base

questions.q: True or False: 'A town that grew from 1.2 lakh people to 1.5 lakh people grew by the same percentage as a village that grew from 2,400 people to 3,000 people.' Give a reason.
questions.a: True. Town: increase 0.3 lakh, and 0.3/1.2 x 100 = 25%. Village: increase 600, and 600/2400 x 100 = 25%. The town gained far more people, but both grew by 25% of their original size.

questions.q:
Two school kabaddi teams record their wins.
Team A: won 18 of 24 matches last season and 21 of 30 matches this season.
Team B: won 12 of 20 matches last season and 18 of 24 matches this season.
(a) Find each team's percentage of matches won in each season.
(b) Which team's winning percentage went down even though its number of wins went up? By what percentage did that team's number of wins increase?
(c) Explain how that team's winning percentage can fall while its number of wins rises.
(d) Over the two seasons together, which team has the better winning percentage? (Round to two decimal places.)
questions.a: (a) Team A: 75% last season, 70% this season. Team B: 60% last season, 75% this season. (b) Team A: its winning percentage fell from 75% to 70%, while its wins rose from 18 to 21, an increase of 3/18 x 100 = 16.67%. (c) Team A played more matches this season (30 against 24), so 21 wins is a smaller share of its matches than 18 of 24 was. (d) Team A: 39 of 54 = 72.22%. Team B: 30 of 44 = 68.18%. Team A has the better two-season record.
s: Part (b): Team A, whose wins rose by 16.67%
Part (c): more matches played, so a smaller share

Show that the number of students in a club cannot decrease by more than 100%, although it can increase by more than 100%. Use the formula for percentage change and one example of each.
questions.a: Percentage decrease = decrease / original x 100. The largest possible decrease is the whole original (everyone leaves), which gives original/original x 100 = 100%; going lower would need fewer than zero students. An increase has no such limit: a club growing from 20 to 70 students increases by 50/20 x 100 = 250%.

Gives an increase of more than 100%, e.g. 20 to 70 = 250%

questions.q: After a 20% increase, the monthly rent of a shop is Rs 9,000. The owner's son works out the old rent as 20% less than Rs 9,000. By how much is the son's figure off?
questions.a: Rs 300

questions.q:
A trust gives one scholarship to the better of two students from different schools, who wrote different tests. Student X scored 68 out of 80; her class average was 60 out of 80. Student Y scored 102 out of 120; his class average was 96 out of 120. The trust first compares the students' percentage scores. If these are equal, it chooses the student who is further above her or his own class average, measured as the difference between the student's percentage and the class-average percentage.
(a) Find the percentage score of each student.
(b) Find each class average as a percentage.
(c) Who gets the scholarship? Justify using (a) and (b).
questions.a: (a) X: 68/80 x 100 = 85%. Y: 102/120 x 100 = 85%. The scores are equal. (b) X's class: 60/80 x 100 = 75%. Y's class: 96/120 x 100 = 80%. (c) X's percentage is 85 - 75 = 10 above her class average, and Y's is 85 - 80 = 5 above his. So Student X gets the scholarship.
s: Part (c): X, 10 above her class average against 5

A weavers' co-operative brings handloom sarees to an exhibition. Each saree costs the co-operative Rs 2,800 to make and is marked at Rs 4,200. On the first day it offers a 15% discount. For the last day it must choose between keeping the 15% discount, when it expects to sell 5 sarees, and giving a 25% discount, when it expects to sell 12 sarees.
(a) What is the selling price of a saree at a 15% discount?
(b) What is the profit percentage on cost at a 15% discount?
(c) What is the profit percentage on cost at a 25% discount?
(d) Which discount should the co-operative choose for the last day? Compare the total profit for the day, and say why the lower profit percentage can still be the better choice.
questions.a: (a) 85% of 4200 = Rs 3,570. (b) Profit = 3570 - 2800 = Rs 770, and 770/2800 x 100 = 27.5%. (c) 75% of 4200 = Rs 3,150; profit = Rs 350, and 350/2800 x 100 = 12.5%. s: Part (d): 25% discount; Rs 4,200 against Rs 3,850 in total profit

questions.q: The materials for a stool cost a carpenter Rs 640. He wants a profit of 35% on this cost, but every customer bargains and gets a 10% discount on the marked price. He must mark the stool at Rs ___ (write the number in digits).

Finds total cost Rs 1,50,000 against sales Rs 1,44,000

questions.a: (a) Cost = 120 x 50 = Rs 6,000. He needs 120% of 6000 = Rs 7,200. (b) 90% of 120 = 108 kg. (c) 7200 / 108 = Rs 66.67 a kg (about). Rs 60 a kg would give a 20% profit only if all 120 kg were sold; the cost of the spoilt 12 kg must be recovered from the 108 kg that are sold.

questions.q:
A stationer buys pens at Rs 24 each and sells them at a profit of 25%. She sells files at Rs 63 each, which gives her a 40% profit on what she paid for them.
(a) At what price does she sell a pen?
(b) What did she pay for a file?
(c) In one week she sells 150 pens and 120 files. What is her total profit?

questions.a: (a) 125% of 24 = Rs 30. (b) 140% of cost = 63, so cost = 63 x 100/140 = Rs 45. (c) Profit = 150 x (30 - 24) + 120 x (63 - 45) = 900 + 2160 = Rs 3,060. (d) Total cost = 150 x 24 + 120 x 45 = 3600 + 5400 = Rs 9,000, so the profit is 3060/9000 x 100 = 34%. It lies between the two rates because it combines a 25% profit on Rs 3,600 of pens with a 40% profit on Rs 5,400 of files; more of the money is in files, so it is nearer to 40%.
s: Part (d): 34%, between 25% and 40%, nearer 40% as more money is in files

questions.a: (a) 48/700 x 100 = 6.86% (about), not 12%. (b) 12% of 700 = 0.12 x 700 = Rs 84. The bill printed Rs 48, the digits of 84 reversed. (c) 700 + 84 = Rs 784. By insisting, the school saves 714 - 705.60 = Rs 8.40 (12% of the Rs 70 discount).
s: Part (d): GST on Rs 630 gives Rs 705.60, saving Rs 8.40

(b) He sells fresh rice, bought at the same price per kg, at a profit of 15%. His helper says the fresh rice is therefore 30% dearer per kg than the old rice was. Is the helper right? Show.
questions.a: (a) 85% of the cost = Rs 850, so the cost = 850 x 100/85 = Rs 1,000 for 25 kg, which is Rs 40 a kg. (b) No. Old rice sold at 850/25 = Rs 34 a kg; fresh rice sells at 115% of 40 = Rs 46 a kg. The difference of Rs 12 is 12/34 x 100 = 35.29% of the old price, not 30%, because the two 15% figures are measured on the cost price, not on Rs 34.
s: Part (a): Rs 40 a kg (Rs 1,000 for 25 kg)

(c) Find the net profit as a percentage of sales in each month.
(d) The owner judges a month by its net profit as a percentage of sales. Which month was better by this measure, even though the other month earned more rupees?
questions.a: (a) Month 1: 90,000 - 54,000 = Rs 36,000. Month 2: 1,20,000 - 78,000 = Rs 42,000. (b) Month 1: 36,000 - 9,000 = Rs 27,000. Month 2: 42,000 - 12,000 = Rs 30,000. (c) Month 1: 27000/90000 x 100 = 30%. Month 2: 30000/120000 x 100 = 25%. (d) Month 1 was better (30% against 25%); Month 2 earned Rs 3,000 more net profit, but on much larger sales.

questions.q: True or False: 'For the same principal and the same annual rate, the amount after exactly 1 year is the same with compounding and without compounding.' Give a reason.
questions.a: True. In both cases the interest for the first year is r x p on the original principal, so the amount after 1 year is p(1 + r) either way (p(1 + r x 1) = p(1 + r)^1). The two options differ only from the second year on.
s: Shows both give p(1 + r) after one year

questions.q: Kavya deposits an amount p for 5 years at 7% p.a., and the interest is added back to the deposit every year. Which expression gives the amount she gets back?

(a) Which scheme gives more after 2 years, and by how much?
(b) Which gives more after just 1 year? Use (a) to say what this shows about a higher rate against compounding.
questions.a: (a) X: 40000 x 1.08 x 1.08 = Rs 46,656. Y: 40000 x (1 + 0.083 x 2) = Rs 46,640. X gives Rs 16 more. (b) After 1 year: X gives 40000 x 1.08 = Rs 43,200 and Y gives 40000 x 1.083 = Rs 43,320, so Y is ahead by Rs 120. Compounding gives nothing extra in the first year; from the second year interest is also earned on interest, and here that is enough to overtake Y's higher rate.
s: Part (b): Y after 1 year (43,320 against 43,200); compounding overtakes only later

questions.q: A deposit grew to Rs 8,100 in 2 years at 12.5% p.a., with the interest added back every year. The amount deposited was Rs ___ (write the number in digits).
A cupboard loses 25% of its value every year. Show that its value can never become zero, however many years pass, and write its value after t years for a starting value of V.
questions.a: Each year the value is multiplied by 1 - 0.25 = 0.75, so after t years it is V x (0.75)^t. Every year 75% of the current value remains; 75% of a positive amount is always positive. A product of positive numbers can never be 0, so the value keeps getting smaller but never reaches zero.
s: Each year multiplies the value by 0.75
Argues a positive amount times 0.75 stays positive, so never zero

questions.q:
A town of 80,000 people grows by 5% every year. A nearby village of 12,500 people shrinks by 4% every year.
(a) Find the town's population after 1, 2 and 3 years.
(b) Find the village's population after 3 years, to the nearest whole number.
(c) A councillor says the village will shrink by 3 x 4% = 12% in 3 years. By what percentage does it actually shrink? (Round to two decimal places.)
(d) A planner assumed the town would grow by a fixed 4,000 people a year (5% of 80,000). By how many people does his 3-year figure fall short, and why does the gap grow each year?
questions.a: (a) 80000 x 1.05 = 84,000; 84000 x 1.05 = 88,200; 88200 x 1.05 = 92,610. (b) 12500 x 0.96 = 12,000; 12000 x 0.96 = 11,520; 11520 x 0.96 = 11,059.2, about 11,059. (c) Fall = 12,500 - 11,059.2 = 1,440.8, and 1440.8/12500 x 100 = 11.53%, less than 12%, because each later 4% is taken on a smaller population. (d) The planner gets 80,000 + 3 x 4,000 = 92,000, which is 92,610 - 92,000 = 610 short. The real yearly growth is 4,000, then 4,200, then 4,410, because each 5% is taken on the larger population of the year before, so the gap grows each year.

questions.q: Lata deposits Rs 10,000 at 10% p.a., and the interest is added back to the deposit every year. How much interest is added in the third year alone?

The population of a village is 3,200, and it falls by about 10% every decade.
(a) What is the expected population after 2 decades?
(b) A survey worker simply takes away 20% of 3,200. How far off is his estimate, and why?
questions.a: (a) 3200 x 0.9 = 2,880 after one decade; 2880 x 0.9 = 2,592 after two. (b) He gets 3200 x 0.8 = 2,560, which is 32 too low. The second 10% fall is taken on 2,880, not on 3,200, so fewer people are lost.
s: Part (b): 2,560 is 32 too low, as the second fall is on 2,880

questions.q:
An amount p is deposited at an annual rate r (written as a decimal) for t years.
(a) Write an expression for the total interest earned when the interest is paid out every year.
(b) Write an expression for the total interest earned when it is compounded every year.
(c) Evaluate both for p = Rs 5,000, r = 0.06 and t = 2.
questions.a: (a) Interest = p x r x t (the amount p(1 + rt) minus the principal p). (b) Interest = p(1 + r)^t - p. (c) Paid out: 5000 x 0.06 x 2 = Rs 600. Compounded: 5000 x 1.06^2 - 5000 = 5618 - 5000 = Rs 618.

questions.a: A 4% loss

questions.q:
The price of a kilogram of cashews rises by 25%.
(a) By what percentage must the new price fall to bring it back to the old price?
(b) If instead the new price falls by 25%, is the final price above or below the old price, and by what percentage?
questions.a: (a) New price = 1.25 x old. To return to old, the fall is 0.25 of 1.25, that is 0.25/1.25 x 100 = 20%. (b) Below: 1.25 x 0.75 = 0.9375, so the final price is 93.75% of the old price, which is 6.25% below it.

questions.q: A jacket is sold at a 25% discount on its marked price, and then 12% GST is added to the discounted price. As a single percentage, the customer pays ___% of the marked price (write the number in digits).

A tea stall sells 400 cups a day at Rs 15 a cup, and each cup costs the owner Rs 8 to make. He is thinking about two plans.
Plan 1: raise the price by 20%; he expects the number of cups sold to fall by 15%.
Plan 2: cut the price by 10%; he expects the number of cups sold to rise by 15%.
(a) Under Plan 1, what are his daily takings, and by what percentage do they change?
(b) Under Plan 2, what are his daily takings, and by what percentage do they change?
(c) A friend says Plan 1 changes the takings by 20% - 15% = +5%. Explain the mistake.
(d) The owner wants the most money left each day after paying for the tea he makes. Which plan should he choose? Show the money left under each plan.
questions.a: (a) Price = 1.2 x 15 = Rs 18; cups = 0.85 x 400 = 340; takings = 18 x 340 = Rs 6,120, against Rs 6,000 now, a 2% increase (1.2 x 0.85 = 1.02). (b) Price = 0.9 x 15 = Rs 13.50; cups = 1.15 x 400 = 460; takings = Rs 6,210, a 3.5% increase (0.9 x 1.15 = 1.035). (c) The 15% fall acts on the number of cups, and the takings are price x cups, so the changes multiply as factors (1.2 x 0.85 = 1.02); they cannot be added. (d) Money left per day: now 400 x 7 = Rs 2,800; Plan 1: 340 x (18 - 8) = Rs 3,400; Plan 2: 460 x (13.50 - 8) = Rs 2,530. He should choose Plan 1: Plan 2 brings in more takings, but each cup leaves only Rs 5.50, so the extra cups do not make up for it.
s: Part (c): the changes multiply as factors 1.2 x 0.85, they do not add
Part (d): Plan 1, Rs 3,400 left against Rs 2,530

questions.q: A sweet shop's banner says: '30% + 20% off on all boxes: that is half price!' Check the banner using a box marked Rs 500.
questions.a: The banner is wrong. After 30% off: 0.7 x 500 = Rs 350. After a further 20% off: 0.8 x 350 = Rs 280. Half price would be Rs 250. The customer pays 0.7 x 0.8 = 0.56 = 56% of the marked price, a total discount of 44%, because the 20% is taken on the reduced price.
s: Compares with half price Rs 250 (44% off, not 50%)
Verdict: wrong; the second discount acts on the reduced price

questions.q: True or False: 'If the length of a rectangle is increased by 10% and its breadth is decreased by 10%, its area stays the same.' Give a reason.
questions.a: False. New area = (1.1 x length) x (0.9 x breadth) = 0.99 x the old area. The area decreases by 1%, because the 10% cut acts on the breadth while the length is already larger.
s: Shows the new area is 0.99 of the old, a 1% decrease

questions.q: A pair of shoes is marked Rs 600. Shop A gives '40% + 10% off' (40% off, then 10% off the reduced price), while Shop B gives a flat 50% off. How much more does the pair cost at Shop A than at Shop B?
questions.a: Rs 24

questions.q:
A shopkeeper marked a cooler 25% above what it cost him. In a sale he gave a 20% discount on the marked price, and then 18% GST was added to the discounted price. The customer paid Rs 2,832.
(a) What was the price after the discount, before GST?
(b) What was the marked price?
(c) What had the cooler cost the shopkeeper?
(d) Compare the price before GST with his cost: did he make a profit or a loss? Explain why a 25% markup followed by a 20% discount gives this result, while a 20% markup followed by a 20% discount does not.
questions.a: (a) 1.18 x price = 2832, so the price before GST = 2832 / 1.18 = Rs 2,400. (b) 0.8 x marked price = 2400, so the marked price = 2400 / 0.8 = Rs 3,000. (c) 1.25 x cost = 3000, so the cost = 3000 / 1.25 = Rs 2,400. (d) No profit and no loss: the price before GST (Rs 2,400) equals the cost. The factors multiply: 1.25 x 0.8 = 1, so the two changes cancel exactly. With a 20% markup, 1.2 x 0.8 = 0.96, a 4% loss, because the 20% discount is taken on the larger marked price.
s: Part (d): no profit, no loss since 1.25 x 0.8 = 1, while 1.2 x 0.8 = 0.96

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
Statement 1: Successive discounts of 10% and then 20% give the same final price as 20% and then 10%.
Statement 2: A 25% increase followed by a 20% decrease brings a price back to where it started.
Statement 3: Two successive increases of 10% are the same as a single increase of 20%.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 and 2 only

questions.q:
A shirt is marked Rs 800. A shop is running a 20% sale, and a customer also has a coupon for Rs 100 off.
(a) Find what she pays if the coupon is used first and then the 20% is taken off, and if the 20% is taken off first and then the coupon is used.
(b) Which order should she ask for? Explain why the order matters here, although it does not matter for two percentage discounts.
questions.a: (a) Coupon first: (800 - 100) x 0.8 = Rs 560. Sale first: 800 x 0.8 - 100 = Rs 540. (b) She should ask for the 20% first, which saves Rs 20 more. Two percentage discounts are both multiplications, which can be done in any order, but a flat Rs 100 is a subtraction: taking the 20% first applies it to the full Rs 800 instead of to Rs 700, and 20% of the extra Rs 100 is the Rs 20.
s: Part (a): Rs 560 with the coupon first, Rs 540 with the sale first
Part (b): 20% first; a flat amount is subtracted, so the order changes the base of the 20%

questions.q:
A shopkeeper marked all his cookware 40% above what he paid for it. To clear old stock, he then gave a 25% discount on the marked price.
(a) Did he make a profit or a loss, and what percentage of his cost?
(b) In the sale he received Rs 10,500. What had those goods cost him?
(c) What discount on the marked price would have given him no profit and no loss? (Round to two decimal places.)
questions.a: (a) Let the cost be x. Marked price = 1.4x; after 25% off, the price is 0.75 x 1.4x = 1.05x, a 5% profit. (b) 1.05x = 10,500, so x = Rs 10,000. (c) He needs 1.4x - d x 1.4x = x, so 1 - d = 1/1.4 and d = 0.4/1.4 = 2/7, about 28.57%.

questions.q:
A city's metro fare between two stations changed as shown.
Year | Fare
2022 | Rs 50
2023 | 8% more than in 2022
2024 | 10% more than in 2023
2025 | 5% less than in 2024
The transport board had promised that the fare would not rise by more than 12.9% over the three years from 2022 to 2025.
(a) What was the fare in 2023?
(b) What was the fare in 2024?
(c) What was the fare in 2025?
(d) A commuter says, '8 + 10 - 5 = 13, so the rise is exactly 13%.' Find the actual overall percentage change and decide whether the board kept its promise.
questions.a: (a) 1.08 x 50 = Rs 54. (b) 1.1 x 54 = Rs 59.40. (c) 0.95 x 59.40 = Rs 56.43. (d) Overall rise = 56.43 - 50 = Rs 6.43, and 6.43/50 x 100 = 12.86%. The commuter's 13% wrongly adds the changes; each acts on the previous year's fare. 12.86% is not more than 12.9%, so the board kept its promise, although the commuter's added-up 13% would wrongly say it was broken.
s: Part (d): 12.86%, so the 12.9% promise was kept (the added-up 13% would say broken)

True or False: 'For an item priced at Rs 5,000, giving a 10% discount and then adding 18% GST gives the same final price as adding 18% GST first and then giving the 10% discount.' Give a reason.
questions.a: True. Discount first: 5000 x 0.9 = 4500, then 4500 x 1.18 = Rs 5,310. GST first: 5000 x 1.18 = 5900, then 5900 x 0.9 = Rs 5,310. Both are 5000 x 0.9 x 1.18, and the order of multiplying does not change the product.
s: Shows both orders give 5000 x 0.9 x 1.18 = Rs 5,310

questions.q: Write a shopping situation that matches the calculation 1500 x 0.8 x 0.9 = 1080, saying what each number stands for. Then explain why the total discount is not 30%.
questions.a: Example: a bedsheet marked Rs 1,500 gets a festival discount of 20% (pay 0.8 of the price), and then a further 10% off the reduced price with a store card (pay 0.9 of that). The customer pays Rs 1,080. The total discount is 1500 - 1080 = Rs 420, which is 420/1500 x 100 = 28%, not 30%, because the 10% is taken on Rs 1,200, not on Rs 1,500.
s: A situation with Rs 1,500, a 20% discount and then a 10% discount
Shows the total discount is 28% and why

questions.q:
Store X sells a phone priced at Rs 15,000. It gives a 20% festival discount, then a further 5% off the reduced price for paying by card, and then adds 18% GST on the final discounted price. Store Y sells the same phone at Rs 15,000 with a single 25% discount and then adds 18% GST.
(a) What is the price at Store X after both discounts, before GST?
(b) What single percentage discount is Store X's pair of discounts equal to?
(c) What does the phone cost at Store X including GST?
(d) Which store is cheaper including GST, and by how much? Explain why, using (b).

(d) Store Y: 15000 x 0.75 = 11,250, then 11250 x 1.18 = Rs 13,275. Store Y is cheaper by 13,452 - 13,275 = Rs 177, because its 25% discount is larger than Store X's combined 24%.
s: Part (d): Store Y, by Rs 177, as 25% beats the combined 24%

A mall had 2,500 visitors a week in September. Its weekly footfall then changed by +20% in October, -10% in November and -10% in December. The manager says: 'The changes add up to 0%, so footfall is back to September's level. Also, we would have ended at the same level whatever order the three changes came in.' Check both parts of the claim, and find the percentage rise needed in January to get back to 2,500.
questions.a: Partly right. October: 2500 x 1.2 = 3,000; November: 3000 x 0.9 = 2,700; December: 2700 x 0.9 = 2,430, which is 2.8% below September (1.2 x 0.9 x 0.9 = 0.972). So the first part is wrong: each change acts on the previous month's footfall, so the changes cannot be added. The second part is right: the factors 1.2, 0.9 and 0.9 give the same product in any order. January needs a rise of 70 on 2,430, which is 70/2430 x 100 = 2.88%.
s: Finds December footfall 2,430 (factor 0.972), so the first part is wrong
Says the second part is right, as the factors can be multiplied in any order
Verdict partly right, and a January rise of 2.88%

questions.q:
A furniture dealer marks chairs 50% above his cost. In a sale he gives 30% off the marked price and sells 10 chairs for Rs 21,000 in all. All the chairs cost him the same. He has 15 chairs left. He can either sell all 15 in the sale at 30% off, or sell all 15 to a school that offers the marked price minus a flat Rs 800 per chair.
(a) What percentage of his cost does he get for a chair in the sale?
(b) What did one chair cost him, and what is its marked price?
(c) Which way of selling the 15 chairs gives him more profit, and by how much?
questions.a: (a) 1.5 x 0.7 = 1.05, so 105% of the cost (a 5% profit). (b) 10 chairs: 1.05 x cost = 21,000, so the cost of 10 chairs = Rs 20,000 and one chair costs Rs 2,000. Marked price = 1.5 x 2000 = Rs 3,000. (c) Sale: 15 x 0.7 x 3000 = Rs 31,500, profit Rs 1,500. School: 15 x (3000 - 800) = Rs 33,000, profit Rs 3,000. Selling to the school gives Rs 1,500 more profit.
s: Part (b): cost Rs 2,000, marked price Rs 3,000
Part (c): the school offer, by Rs 1,500
